title: What does NFTokenBurn do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of NFTokenBurn and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, NFTokenBurn permanently removes an NFT from the ledger under its ownership and burn-permission rules. [1]

The owner can burn a token, and an issuer or authorized minter has additional powers only where the token's capabilities allow them. The NFTokenID identifies the exact token. Burning removes ledger ownership but cannot erase copies of an image or revoke every off-ledger contractual right associated with it. [1]

The NFTokenBurn reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using NFTokenBurn, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
